name: Toe sleeve (toe initiator)
function: The pressure-actuated sleeve at the toe of the lateral that opens the first path to the formation without a wireline run, so the first stage can be pumped and the tool string pumped down for stage two.

tabs.overview: Cemented in with the casing at the toe; a pressure cycle above the casing test pressure opens its ports. Without it the first stage would need tractor-conveyed or coiled tubing perforating because there is no flow path to pump the string down. In the simulator the toe sleeve is stage 1 of a sliding sleeve job: the casing is pressured with the pumps at a low rate until the ports open and the pressure drops. tabs.engineering: Opening pressure set above the casing test pressure with a margin; often a time delay or a rupture disc.
tabs.connections: Threaded into the casing string near the toe.
tabs.safety: The casing test and the sleeve opening pressure must be sequenced correctly.
tabs.evidence: Public plug-and-perf explainer (S20), API Spec 11D1 scope (S21), field practice (S9). Dimensions are public example values, not a manufacturer's design.
tabs.operations: Opened before the first stage; used once.
tabs.failure_modes: Opening during the casing test, failing to open, cement in the ports.
